Universal Controller

Fieldbus controller — with Ethernet · all lines ESTIMATE
MCU card: STM32C5A3VGT6 (144 MHz, Ethernet, 2× CAN-FD, crypto, no
TrustZone) ≈ 300 + 16 MB QSPI NOR (log + OTA) + RTC with CR2032
Ethernet on the MCU card: LAN8720AI + 25 MHz crystal + RJ45 with
magnetics ≈ 200 (owner figure), ESD + passives ≈ 70
6 analog inputs, each 0–10 V / 4–20 mA / PT1000: op-amps, 0.1 %
resistors, mode FETs, protection, 0.1 % 2.5 V reference
10 digital inputs: single optocouplers (LTV-217 / EL3H7 class), IEC
8 relays SPDT 10 A, 230 VAC / 30 VDC, 5 kV reinforced, INR 40 each (owner
target); ULN2803, watchdog gating, snubbers
Fuse per relay: 5×20 mm 10 A time-lag in a front-access holder, INR 20
each incl. holder (owner)
4 high-side 24 V outputs: TPS274160B quad ≈ 144 (PWM ≈ 1–2 kHz), current
sense, TVS, reverse FET
4 low-side 24 V outputs (2026-11-24): quad driver, TI DRV8803 class (60
V, 2 A, protected), TVS, 4 poles, 4 LEDs
Motor-driver provision (2026-11-24): footprints for 2 × DRV8873S — 2
motors or 4 half-bridges; not fitted, option
24 relay terminal poles, 5.08 mm, 300 V / 10 A, kept apart from the low-
voltage terminals

109, protection, switchable termination, terminal
USB-C service port (5 V, no PD) + LEDs
4-pin bus connectors, bridge share, bus RS-485 transceiver, ESD
36 fixed 3.81 mm screw terminals, shared analog common (≈ 2 per pole)
Base card PCB, 4-layer

DC-DC + power stage on the base card, feeding the MCU card: buck to 5 V +

Passives
IO status LEDs: 6 AI, 10 DI, 8 relays, 4 high-side (≈ 1.5 each)
Enclosure: off-the-shelf PLC-style DIN housing ≈ 90 mm, V-0 (D-37; part
from the fit study)

Notes
• LoRa selling price INR 1,600 (owner, 2026-11-19), read as price after profit without battery board and adapter: needs
a BOM of ≤ INR 687 at 100 pcs, now 1,154 — a 40 % cut.
• With Ethernet (default), incl. power stage and enclosure: 3,104 (limit INR 2,000: over by 1,104); low-cost build
without Ethernet: 2,827.
• MCU: two plug-in MCU cards on one base-card interface (owner, 2026-11-24) — STM32C5A3VGT6 standard (no TrustZone),
STM32H573VIT6 option (PSA L3); low-cost build without Ethernet on STM32H523VET6 as an option; motor drivers are a
provision, fitted to order. PIC32CK dropped (120 MHz, no Zephyr drivers). LoRa redesigned as a remote IO node (owner,
2026-11-19): STM32WLE5 at INR 250, 2-layer PCB, 16 MB QSPI NOR for its own OTA and logging (2026-11-23), RS-485 + 4 DI
+ 4 AI + 4 DO (low-power high-side quad), SMA antenna kept for long range — BOM 1,154. Tip: volume quotes (≈ −10 %) →
≈ 1,039; no relays: their coils would drain the battery.
• Tip — every module: this is a high-volume product, so negotiate the big parts with distributors (modem, ESP32-C6
module, MCUs, isolated transceivers, enclosures); the BOMs here are still research prices × 1.3 at 100 units.
• Adapter (owner, 2026-11-18): one 12 V 18 W adapter per stack or standalone module; a full 4-module stack peaks at ≈
13–14 W with charging capped at 0.3 A per battery board.
• Not included: development amortisation — at 100 pieces every INR 1 lakh of NRE per module type adds INR 1,000 to its
cost and ≈ INR 1,300 to its price after profit; distributor margin (left to the client / partner).
